newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-FRENCH QUALIFIER BLOWS AWAY ZVEREVA.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-FRENCH QUALIFIER BLOWS AWAY ZVEREVA.

text.p: French qualifier Sarah Pitkowksi inflicted the indignity of a "double bagel" defeat on former title-holder Natasha Zvereva on Monday in the first round of the Sydney International tennis tournament.
Zvereva was thrashed 6-0 6-0 by Pitkowski, who said later she was surprised by the ease of her victory.
"She was slow," Pitkowski said. "I saw she was so slow so I took a chance and tried to keep my cool...But she helped me a lot because she didn't play very well at all."

In the men's singles at the same tournament, top seed Goran Ivanisevic made short work of Germany's Marc-Kevin Goellner, beating him 6-3 6-4 in the first round and converting his second match point with a trademark ace.

Pitkowski, 21, moved to Paris from the north of France six years ago to attend the National Tennis Centre at Roland Garros and is becoming more of a regular fixture on the tour. Her highest ranking was 84.
Zvereva, a 25-year-old from Belarus, was on the receiving end of one of the more famous 6-0 6-0 score-lines in tennis history when she was blanked by Steffi Graf in the 1988 French Open final.
In other women's singles matches, Kimberly Po of the United States ousted Austrian veteran Judith Wiesner 6-2 3-6 6-4 and Canada's Rene Simpson downed sixth seed Karina Habsudova of Slovakia 6-4 7-5.

Ivanisevic, beaten in last year's final by U.S. player Todd Martin, said he was pleased with his form ahead of next week's Australian Open in Melbourne, the first Grand Slam tournamernt of the season.
"I'm moving very well and I'm not missing too many balls," the world number three told reporters. "My service is not 100 percent there yet, it can still improve.
"I did hit a couple of good serves there in the end, but it's the first tournament, the first match, and it's important I put all these things together for next week," he said.

Third seed Albert Costa breezed past Frenchman Lionel Roux 6-4 6-2 after Roux came into the main draw as a lucky loser following the late withdrawal of hard-serving Australian Mark Philippoussis with tendinitis in his forearm.
